definition: A simple chart of a chip's attainable speed: the lower of its peak compute (a flat roof) and its memory bandwidth times the work's arithmetic intensity (a sloped line). It shows at a glance whether a workload is limited by compute or by memory.
The arithmetic intensity at which a chip switches from memory-bound to compute-bound: peak FLOPS divided by memory bandwidth. About 295 FLOPs per byte for an H100 in dense BF16.
A workload whose speed is limited by how fast data can be read from memory rather than by how fast the chip can calculate; adding FLOPS does not help, adding bandwidth does.
A workload whose speed is limited by the chip's arithmetic throughput because it reuses each byte many times; adding memory bandwidth does not help.
The matrix-multiplication operation that accounts for most of the arithmetic in neural networks. Large GEMMs have high arithmetic intensity and run near a GPU's peak FLOPS.
A hardware trick in which two of every four weights are zero so the tensor cores can skip them, doubling quoted peak FLOPS. Headline NVIDIA figures often assume it; dense figures do not.
The rule that the part of a job that cannot be sped up (in AI clusters, usually communication that cannot overlap with compute) caps the total speed-up from adding processors.
A low-latency, lossless networking standard used for scale-out AI clusters; NVIDIA became its leading supplier through the 2020 Mellanox acquisition (Quantum switches, ConnectX adapters).
NVIDIA's Ethernet platform for AI clusters, pairing Spectrum switches with SuperNICs and adaptive routing to approach InfiniBand-like performance on Ethernet.
Removing heat with liquid circulated through cold plates on the chips rather than with air; required for racks of roughly 100 kW and above such as the GB200 NVL72.
NVIDIA's plan (from 2027) to distribute 800-volt direct current to racks, cutting conversion steps and copper so a single rack can draw up to about a megawatt.
Total facility power divided by the power used by the IT equipment; 1.0 would mean zero overhead for cooling and power conversion.
